newsitem.title: USA: 15 vie for governor's seat in Wash. state primary.
newsitem.headline: 15 vie for governor's seat in Wash. state primary.

text.p: Washington state voters face a dizzying array of choices in a primary election Tuesday that features 15 candidates for the open governor's seat and several hotly contested congressional races.

Democrat Gary Locke and Republican Ellen Craswell were the favourites in the race to succeed outgoing Democratic Gov. Mike Lowry, stepping down after a single term marred by a sexual harassment scandal.

But opinion poll data collected in late August before absentee ballots went out showed 38 percent of likely voters were undecided, said Stuart Elway of Elway Research, who added that the winners might need less than 20 percent of the total vote each under the state's open primary system.
"So far most voters are trying to get to know all of these people, and there's a lot of them," said.

While none of the state's nine incumbent congressmen faced challenges within their own party, there were several hard-fought primary races, particularly among Democrats seeking to unseat Republican freshmen.

Washington, traditionally a swing state, was considered a key battleground as Democrats worked to reverse one of the Republican Party's biggest victories of its 1994 sweep, when six of the state's congressional seats changed over to Republican hands.
Republican freshmen Reps. Rick White, Jack Metcalf and Randy Tate were considered most vulnerable in the November elections.

In the gubernatorial race Locke, one of the highest-ranking Asian-American elected officials on the U.S. mainland, faced his stiffest primary challenge from Seattle Mayor Norm Rice, who was seeking to become the state's first black governor.
Locke, a first-generation American of Chinese descent, is executive of King County, which includes Seattle, and therefore he and Rice shared an overlapping core constituency.
Also in the hunt for the Democratic nomination was former U.S. Representative Jay Inslee.
Craswell, a former state senator, came from the powerful Christian conservative wing of the state's Republican party and has pledged a return of government to higher moral values.
Her toughest challenges come from King County Prosecutor Norm Maleng -- the only candidate in the race to have run for statewide election before -- and state House Majority Leader Dale Foreman.
About 70 candidates were running for statewide office, not to mention hundreds more seeking municipal office or seats in the state Legislature.
While Republicans took control of the state House in 1994, political analysts believed President Clinton could lead a return to firm Democratic control of the state legislative branch.

Clinton took Washington state in 1992 despite winning only 43 percent of the popular vote, and he was seen as the clear favourite to beat Republican nominee Bob Dole for the state's 11 electoral votes.
